hook: The philosopher of liberty, whose ideas ended up in the American Declaration of Independence.

pages.x: John Locke was born in 1632 in Somerset, the son of a country lawyer who fought for Parliament in the civil war. He was a schoolboy at Westminster in 1649, when King Charles I was beheaded nearby. He went on to study medicine at Oxford.

In 1666 he met Lord Ashley, later Earl of Shaftesbury, and became his doctor. He saved his patron's life by draining an abscess on his liver through a silver tube, and became his secretary and adviser.
pages.img: Anthony Ashley Cooper, 1st Earl of Shaftesbury

pages.x: Shaftesbury plotted against King Charles II, and Locke fled to the Netherlands in 1683, living under a false name. He came home in 1689, after the Glorious Revolution, on the same ship as the new queen, Mary.

In his Two Treatises of Government he argued that everyone has natural rights to "life, liberty and property", that governments rule only with the consent of the people, and that if a ruler breaks that trust, the people may replace him.
In An Essay Concerning Human Understanding he argued that the mind at birth is a blank slate, and that all our ideas come from experience. The book shaped psychology, education and science.
He also argued for religious toleration: the state should not force anyone's beliefs, because true faith cannot be forced.
Locke is called the father of liberalism. Thomas Jefferson put his ideas into the Declaration of Independence: "life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness".
pts: Said everyone has natural rights to life, liberty and property
Argued that government needs the consent of the people
Inspired the American Declaration of Independence
